observedDefects.likelyCause: A reading of the code, not a fix: FFXBattleHud.clearTransientOverlays() hides .ig-banner on a new command, a turn-start for a different actor, or a state that carries the result. After the last enemy action there is no further command or turn, so the banner waits for the final sync, which lands about 1 s into the victory pose. The same class as the "stale Ronso Rage banner" (2026-09-18).

cardboard.verdict: The per-command moves (M1) never leave the safe cone: no painting in frame is more than 20 deg off the lens, so nothing reads as a card. The side and reverse angles (M4) only work because the mock turns each plane to face the lens for that shot, a per-shot billboard the engine does not have (its eased yaw stops at 26 deg, clamped at 34 deg off the camera). Without it the side shot squeezes the party to about 60 % width and the reverse shows every painting mirrored. No painting swap happens in stage 1, so there is no swap pop yet.
cardboard.stage2: Rear paintings: every SHARP figure in every M2/M3/M6 shot is within 27 deg of the lens (m2Swaps.measuredAnglesPerShot); the one squeezed card is Chapter I Attack’s Yuna (-49 deg), half out of frame. M4 side angles now need no plane turned (7-31 deg); the reverse angles still do (party and boss turned square to the lens; untouched, the boss plane sits 116-141 deg off the lens, i.e. its back, mirrored and squeezed to 44-56 %). M5 is billboards throughout. Swaps: no pop in any cut or whip (m2Swaps); the M5 swaps happen under the column.

whatHappened: M2/M1/M0 Chapter IV (the same timeline, deterministic): Bahamut takes his turn at 6.92 s while the top-level list is up (after Esc at 6.55 s), hits Rikku at 7.81 s; the player opens Item at 8.0 s, so the tail of his attack and its numeral play into the Item shot (the shoulder shot in M2).

M3 Chapter IV: Bahamut's attack starts at 0.28 s under Yuna's top-level list and lands at 1.17 s, after the camera has gone behind Yuna for her White Magic list; later Yuna's Cure plays while Paine's menu opens (the turn cut-in at about 4 s).

M5: filmed inside the Skill list, where Wait holds: nothing acts.
ffx2Clock.underWait: The shoulder shots open with a submenu or the target cursor, and that is exactly where Wait holds the clock: no fiend can START acting while the camera is behind a girl. A fiend starts only at the top level, which in M2 is the master (wide) shot, the frame PR-0150 wants. The only overlap is an action that started at the top level and is still playing when the player opens a submenu (the Item beat above).
ffx2Clock.underActive: The clock also runs in submenus and the target cursor, so a fiend can start and finish a whole action while the camera sits behind a girl with a list or the reticle up. That is the case PR-0150 fixed (src/engine/TargetFrameHold.ts: the shot grammar pushed in on the attacker, the party was framed out, the reticle sat on a camera that had moved under it; the approved targeting tile docs/concepts/targeting/b-ring-and-dim/s3.png is a WIDE frame). A per-command camera under Active needs one of: (a) hold the shoulder framing through the enemy action (the attacker may be out of frame and the hit lands on a girl behind the camera, like the numeral in the Item beat), (b) cut back to the wide frame for every enemy action under an open menu (the camera leaves the player's decision mid-choice), and in both cases re-project the reticle every frame of any move (the mock does this; the live HUD only re-projects it on a selection change). Chapter I is FFX (CTB): no clock runs during a menu, so none of this arises.

ffx-ch1.cut: The rear paintings go in on the cut frame itself, so there is nothing to see swap: each cut is one frame-difference spike of 24-36 (mean absolute difference, 0-255) and the next frames settle at 0.5-2.5 (sway and snow). No pop. It reads as coverage in a film edit: the view changes and the figures are their backs from the first frame.
ffx-ch1.whip: A 0.32 s whip pan with a horizontal motion blur that peaks at mid-move; the paintings swap on that frame. The frame-difference curve stays smooth through each whip (8-26, no spike at the swap), so no pop is visible. The target reticle is hidden during the whip and redrawn on landing.

ffx2-ch4.cut: Same as Chapter I: one spike per cut (22-43), then 0.3-4 (the 2-4 after the Item cut is Bahamut's hit numeral and the focus rack starting). No pop.
ffx2-ch4.whip: Smooth frame-difference curves through every whip (9-31), no spike at the swap frames, no pop. At 8.0 s the whip into Item starts while Bahamut's hit on Rikku is landing, so its numeral rides the blur.

m2Swaps.whichReadsBetter: The HARD CUT. Both hide the swap completely, so the choice is about reading the game: the cut is legible on its first frame (menu, reticle and figures), costs no time, and reads like authored coverage. The whip spends 0.32 s of illegible blur on every command change, six times in 11 s, and gets tiring on Esc and re-open. Keep the whip for one beat if it is kept at all: the first command of a new turn, or the confirm into an action.

measuredAnglesPerShot.note: degOffLens: the angle between a painted plane and the lens after the engine's own eased yaw settles (0 = square on); widthKept = cos of it. shareInFrame: how much of the figure's projected box is in frame. Figures behind the camera (Chapter IV Item: Yuna 147, Rikku 129; Attack: Yuna 98) project badly and are not in the picture. Every SHARP figure in every M2 shot is within 27 degrees of the lens; the one squeezed card is Chapter I Attack's Yuna (-49 deg, 65 % width), half out of frame at the right edge.
